title: Association between surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways and postoperative delirium in geriatric hip fracture patients: A retrospective cohort study
content:
by Zixing Zhao, Jinsheng Yu, Yubin Lan, Baitao Yang, Qi Tan, Zaoxiong Wen, Yitao Yao, Cuitian He, Xinyu Fang

Background

Elderly hip fracture patients are at high risk of postoperative delirium (POD). The association between surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways and POD incidence remains poorly clarified. This study aimed to explore the association between surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways, internal fixation clinical pathway(IFCP), versus arthroplasty clinical pathway(ARCP), and POD occurrence in elderly hip fracture patients.

Methods

This retrospective cohort study examined the medical records of patients aged 65 years and older who underwent hip fracture surgery at a tertiary medical facility from January 2022 to December 2025. Patients were divided into groups according to the surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways they received: those with extracapsular fractures who underwent intramedullary nailing were assigned to the IFCP group, and those with intracapsular fractures who underwent hip arthroplasty were assigned to the ARCP group. Multivariate logistic regression and propensity score matching (PSM) analyses were utilized to evaluate the association between surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways and POD. Subgroup analysis was subsequently conducted to explore potential interactions further.

Results

A total of 693 patients were included in this study, with a POD incidence of 15.01% (104/693) during the postoperative hospitalization period. Before matching, the incidence of POD was significantly lower in the ARCP group than in the IFCP group (9.92% vs. 20.61%, P < 0.001). This significant difference persisted after matching (11.54% vs. 18.85%, P = 0.020). Multivariate logistic regression confirmed that the ARCP was independently associated with a reduced risk of POD (OR = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.24–0.67, P < 0.001).

Conclusions

Surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways showed a statistically association with POD risk among elderly hip fracture patients. The ARCP exhibited a lower observed incidence of POD compared with the IFCP.
